sections.heading: Commercial Roof Repair We Provide in Newark, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing repairs 6 commercial roof problems across Essex County: membrane seam separations, punctures and tears, flashing failures at curbs and penetrations, ponding-water damage, blistering and delamination, and storm-opened laps — on low-slope EPDM, TPO, PVC, modified-bitumen, and built-up roofs.

runs.v: Commercial roof repair traces water entry on a low-slope membrane to the failed detail, then reseals it with manufacturer-approved bonding that keeps a system warranty intact.

A commercial low-slope membrane fails most often at the seams: EPDM at the splice seams and TPO at the welded seams, per NRCA technical guidance, while modified bitumen fails at blistering and alligator cracking and PVC at plasticizer-loss embrittlement. A Newark Quality Roofing commercial repair diagnoses the membrane type before sealing the failed component, because EPDM lasts 15 to 25 years, TPO 7 to 20 years, modified bitumen 20 years, BUR 30 years, and PVC 20 to 30 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and Single Ply Roofing Industry data.

c.v: Membrane seam repair

items.v: — Membrane seam repair reseals the splice or welded seam where a low-slope membrane fails most often, because seam separation is the dominant EPDM failure mode and welded-seam failure the dominant TPO failure mode, per NRCA technical guidance.

c.v: Puncture and tear repair

items.v: — Puncture and tear repair patches the impact opening from rooftop traffic, dropped tools, or HVAC service, cutting the patch to size and bonding it with manufacturer-approved adhesive at the correct coverage rate to keep a system warranty intact.

c.v: Flashing repair

items.v: — Flashing repair restores the weather barrier at parapet walls, equipment curbs, drains, and penetrations, where the transition between the field membrane and the vertical surface fails from movement, UV exposure, and material incompatibility, per NRCA technical guidance.

c.v: Ponding-water and drainage repair

items.v: — Ponding-water and drainage repair clears the standing water that breaks down membrane seams, because ponding water remaining more than 48 hours counts as a defect and a flat roof needs at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to drain, per NRCA and ARMA.

c.v: Blister and delamination repair

items.v: — Blister and delamination repair addresses trapped moisture beneath the membrane on modified-bitumen and built-up roofs, where blistering, delamination, and alligator cracking from UV oxidation lift the surface, per NRCA technical guidance.

c.v: Storm-damage membrane repair

items.v: — Storm-damage membrane repair reseals the laps and flashing wind opens, because wind and hail rank as the largest homeowners-insurance claim type at 2.8% of insured homes per year, 1 in 36, per the Insurance Information Institute (Triple-I, 2019–2023).

runs.v: Built-up roofing systems are designed for strength and weather resistance, and modified bitumen roofing adds polymer-modified plies to the same idea, so a repair on either system rebuilds the plies it cuts through rather than smearing a single patch over the top. Every Newark Quality Roofing repair ends with a water test, timestamped photographs, and a record for the building maintenance file.

Emergency leak response should provide rapid patching for active leaks in commercial roofing: a temporary membrane patch at the entry point, a tarp over a torn section, and cleared drains so ponding water stops loading the roof deck, which is part of ensuring structural integrity during a storm.

sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Commercial Roof Repair

runs.v: Leak-Source Diagnosis on Low-Slope Membranes

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing locates the water entry on a commercial low-slope roof with visual membrane inspection, seam probing, core sampling, and infrared moisture scanning, because the leak entry point sits distant from the visible interior evidence.

runs.v: Water on a low-slope roof travels along insulation-board joints, metal-deck flutes, and structural members before reaching a penetration into the occupied space, per NRCA technical guidance, so a core sample checks for wet insulation at the suspect area. An infrared scan locates subsurface wet insulation rather than the breach itself, and ASTM C1153 requires a suspected wet area be verified by core cut, probe, or calibrated moisture meter, per ASTM and the NRCA. Experienced contractors use tools like thermal imaging to detect hidden roof issues across a large roof in one pass, then confirm each wet area before cutting anything out.
Repair to Membrane-Specific Manufacturer Specification

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing matches the repair to the membrane type with manufacturer-approved materials and techniques, because incompatible adhesives, patches, and sealants degrade both the repair and the surrounding membrane.

runs.v: EPDM splice seams join with primer, splice tape, and lap adhesive, TPO and PVC seams weld with hot air, and modified-bitumen patches bond to the base sheet, each to the manufacturer specification that keeps the system warranty intact. A repair to manufacturer specification preserves the material warranty that covers factory defects, separate from the written workmanship warranty that backs the labor, per Owens Corning warranty guidance. Top quality materials only help when the roofing materials are compatible: quality materials from the wrong system still fail at the bond.
Water Testing, Documentation, and NJ Code Compliance

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing water-tests the repair before leaving the site and documents the work, then sizes the repaired area against the NJ permit threshold.

runs.v: A water test verifies the seam, patch, or flashing repair stops the entry, and timestamped photographs and material data record the work for the building maintenance file and any insurance claim. On a commercial building, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires complete removal of a water-soaked covering or a roof already carrying 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.

sections.heading: Repair, Restore, or Replace a Commercial Roof? The 25% Rule

c.v: A commercial roof should be repaired while the damage is localized, restored while the membrane is still sound, and replaced once the damage spreads past the 25% line.

runs.v: Newark Quality Roofing's rule of thumb: replace a commercial roof when membrane damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof area, when a repair approaches 30% of replacement cost, or when leaks recur at the same location. Recurring issues affecting over 25% of a roof's surface typically require full replacement, because at that point the patches are chasing a membrane whose roof performance is spent.

Between repair and replacement sits restoration. Coatings can be applied to aging roofs to extend their lifespan without full replacement, but only over a membrane and insulation that are dry: a core sample or an infrared scan confirms that first, because a coating over wet insulation seals the water in and turns a restoration into a larger tear off later.

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: On a commercial building, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area within a 12-month period takes the work out of ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, so it needs a construction permit and has to meet the current code. Local building codes in Newark, which enforce the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code, dictate specific requirements for roofing work past that line, including the rule that a water-soaked covering or a roof already carrying 2 or more layers comes off completely, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4. When the numbers point to a commercial roof replacement, the tear off, new insulation, and new membrane are priced as a roof installation on their own written scope, a separate roofing project from the repair.

sections.heading: Commercial Roof Inspections and Preventive Maintenance

c.v: Roof inspections assess the entire roofing system for issues — membrane, seams, flashing, drains, and the roof deck — and regular inspections help detect minor issues before they worsen.

runs.v: Annual roof inspections are recommended by experts as a minimum, and commercial low-slope roofs are commonly inspected twice a year, in spring and fall, plus after major storms. A roof inspection can prevent costly repairs in the future: a clogged drain found in October is a cleanup, while the same drain found after a January thaw can mean replacing wet insulation.

Effective commercial roof repairs need to address drainage issues to prevent ponding water, because proper drainage prevents accelerated deterioration of roofing membranes, and regular inspections help avoid emergency disruptions from drainage issues. Scheduled preventative maintenance can help mitigate long-term roofing costs: regular commercial roof maintenance means clearing drains and scuppers, resealing flashing, and fixing small punctures before they become expensive repairs. Comprehensive inspections also protect energy efficiency, because wet insulation loses much of its R-value, and they document the roof's condition for warranties and insurance. Newark Quality Roofing provides free roof inspections on residential and commercial properties across Newark and the surrounding communities of Essex County.

sections.heading: How to Choose Commercial Roofers in Newark, NJ

c.v: The best roof repair contractors in Newark, NJ are registered, insured contractors with hands-on experience on your roof type, and they prove it in writing.

runs.v: Choosing the right roofing contractor requires verifying licensing and insurance, and New Jersey has no separate state roofing license: home improvement contractors, roofing contractors and siding contractors alike, register with the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs, and the Contractors' Registration Act requires commercial general liability insurance of at least $500,000 per occurrence. Roofing contractors should have hands-on experience with specific roofing systems, because an EPDM splice, a TPO weld, and a modified-bitumen patch are three different skills.

It's important to compare multiple contractor bids to get a comprehensive view of options, and contractors should provide detailed written estimates outlining scope, materials, and costs; in New Jersey, a home improvement contract over $500 must be in writing. Asking for local references can help gauge contractor reliability, and for a New Jersey business the best reference is another building owner whose commercial roofing project the contractor handled. Major roofing manufacturers offer certifications for contractors based on performance standards, so ask which manufacturer certifications a roofing contractor actually holds and confirm them with the manufacturer. Verifying safety protocols is crucial for contractors working on commercial roofing sites, where roof edges, skylights, and rooftop equipment put crews and tenants at risk. When comparing commercial roofing services, weigh every bid against those checks: Newark Quality Roofing brings an experienced team with more than 25 years of Newark experience, GAF-certified installers, New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor registration, liability coverage, and free estimates, and reputable roofers offer free inspections before any quote.
